concerns.title: Stefanie Kirschke — XTO, Fasken Evans 11B 2H, air job 35372, 11:08 AM. The OWL narrative records a wellhead leak found and repaired during the job
concerns.text: : "A small leak was identified at the casing valve during the job. The leak was evaluated and the area was monitored while repairs were made." No numeric reading was recorded for the leak event and no permit was uploaded. The handling described is sound — identified early, monitored, repaired before continuing — and the Learn entry is specific. It is listed here because a leaking casing valve is a real condition, not because anything on the form suggests it was handled badly. See the next section for the selection point.

concerns.title: Cindy Smith — XTO, Brunson 34 2, air job 35333, 1:29 PM. The Details field records a benzene detection
concerns.text: : "Work area and bleeder valves tested prior to crew beginning work. No gases detected until 3rd break. A small amount of benzene was detected but CM said it was within range, so no stop work was utilized and crew was able to work without supplied air. Crew replaced parts for frac protection."

A small amount of benzene was detected but CM said it was within range, so no stop work was utilized and crew was able to work without supplied air. Crew replaced parts for frac protection.

confirm.text: This is a gas reading above zero, with the decision not to stop work and not to go to supplied air attributed to the customer's company man rather than to a Canon reading. No numeric value was recorded. Follow-up: ask for the actual benzene reading and confirm whether a Canon-side threshold was applied independently of the company man's call. Pablo Soto worked the same job and his form carries no mention of the detection.
Stop work / unsafe conditions — needs confirmation, not action

None of today's forms selected "Stop work authority utilized". Where a stop-work item appears it is the routine pre-job item "Stop work authority was discussed", which is not a stop-work event. The items below need the technicians' confirmation of what they meant to record; they are not confirmed events.
"Unsafe conditions" selected, no narrative naming a condition — Michael Jobe, three forms in one day:
Shackelford 3B 302H, job 35330, 11:20 AM — "Unsafe conditions" and "Stop work authority was discussed" both selected. Narrative reads only "Went over safety measures with the new crew".
Shackelford Sprayberry Unit 301H, job 35195_1, 11:21 AM — same two items selected. Narrative reads "Was a new crew went over the 12 steps in what safety measures needed to be done".

University 3-12 C 3H, job 35415_1, 3:13 PM — same two items selected. Narrative reads "Had a good meet of what we needed to be done there was a wire line next to us they stop for us to complete the job".

All three forms carry the identical ten-item multi-select string, which points to a selection being carried forward rather than made fresh on each job. Michael Jobe appeared on this list on 09/26/2026 with the same pattern, twice in one day; today is three times. This is the training point Kelby Hammer identified — the technician should confirm whether an actual unsafe condition arose on any of these three jobs.
"Stop work authority was discussed" selected, routine, no issue raised:
1099 Christian Lee — University 3-12 C 3H (35415_2) and Shackelford Sprayberry Unit 301H (35195_2)

Larry Jaramillo — Nail Tillman W1P 416H (35370); his narrative notes "Parts and tools were slippery due to rain waters" and that the crew "Worked slower and more cautious", which reads as a hazard handled rather than a stop-work event
Stefanie Kirschke — Fasken Evans 11B 2H (35372)
Not the mis-selection pattern — two forms where the narrative and the selection point opposite ways:

Stefanie Kirschke, Fasken Evans 11B 2H (35372): the narrative names a real condition — a leak at the casing valve, evaluated and repaired mid-job — but "Unsafe conditions" was not selected. This is the inverse of the Jobe pattern and matches what Jordan Lemmons did on 09/26/2026 with two leaking valves. Cindy Smith, Brunson 34 2 (35333): the narrative records benzene detected and states plainly "no stop work was utilized", yet neither stop-work item nor "Unsafe conditions" was selected. In both cases the written record understates what the form itself describes, which is the opposite risk to over-selection and worth raising with both technicians.

clean.text: Nothing requiring attention from: Larry Jaramillo — two Trailer Inspection Forms for 602 with all photos captured on the day, plus two air job forms with specific narratives including the wet-conditions hazard note. Justin Pack — H2S daily for Lipsey 1H, complete hydro and cascade entries, all photos on the day. Joshua Blassingame — H2S daily for the Lipsey 1H night shift, complete entries, all photos on the day. Michael Jobe's 5:18 AM Trailer Inspection Form for 604 and Rolando Flores's 11:16 AM Trailer Inspection Form for 601, both fully photographed on the day. Andrew Bailey's 8:54 PM Trailer Inspection Form for 602, all photos current. Rolando Flores's two air job forms, which carry the fullest close-out narratives filed today. And both Athena well testing technicians deserve credit on the documentation itself — the gas readings in concern 1 are a problem in the field, but they were

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates, SCBA and workpack checklist entries, cascade gauge readings and 4-gas calibration dates all exist only inside images, not as text, so none of them can be confirmed or ruled out here — only the presence of the photograph and its capture date can.

A second limitation applies to this run specifically. The review ran at 11:00 PM Central on the day being reviewed, so the usual sweep of the following morning's mail for late-arriving submissions could not be performed. Any form for 10/03/2026 filed later that night or the following morning would not appear here, and the two missing Trailer Inspection Forms and two missing supervision dailies should be re-checked against the next day's inbox before anyone is asked about them.
